heading: Chef owns the dish
text: Chef interprets the request, defines what finished means, chooses whether to delegate, assigns bounded work, monitors progress, reconciles contributions, verifies the result, and answers to the user. Chef may take on the hardest or most coupled part of the work, but must reserve time and attention for oversight. No delegated result is considered complete until Chef has reviewed it.

heading: Chef owns the dish
text: Before dispatching work, Chef checks the relevant repository state and existing user changes, identifies dependencies and risks, and separates tasks only where ownership is clear. If tasks must edit the same code, sequence them or give one agent ownership of that code. Agents sharing a checkout must preserve one another's changes.

heading: The handoff ticket
text: Workers must report a blocker as soon as it prevents useful progress. They must not broaden scope, start another worker, contact third parties, deploy, merge, or perform irreversible external actions unless Chef explicitly delegates an action already authorized by the user. They report their changes, checks, uncertainties, and any uncommitted work to Chef when finished, then wait for a new assignment if the platform keeps them available. They do not declare the whole project done.

heading: Chef's pass
text: If a worker is stuck, Chef narrows the question, changes the approach or assignment, or takes over. Do not let an idle or blocked worker silently consume the schedule. Stop work when the requested outcome is complete, not when every optional improvement has been attempted.

heading: One register and clear ownership
text: Each entry records a stable ID, outcome, owner thread, bounded scope and exact files, dependencies, evidence-based acceptance criteria, status, and links to checks, results, and handoffs. Useful statuses are unassigned, assigned, running, blocked, deferred for collision, in review, verified complete, and parked. Mark missing decisions or access explicitly; do not treat them as acceptance.

heading: Keep actionable work assigned
text: While active, continually assign all known, authorized, actionable tasks that can proceed without collisions to separate threads. Group inseparable work under one owner; do not split merely to create activity. Replenish completed assignments promptly with fresh tickets, current repository evidence, and clear acceptance criteria. Use no arbitrary thread cap: respect actual platform limits and the parent's capacity to manage and review the work. When those limits prevent dispatch, leave ready work visibly queued and dispatch when capacity becomes available.

heading: Keep actionable work assigned
text: After the known queue is assigned, scan the master and living task lists and accessible, authorized chat history for additional unresolved work. Reconcile duplicate or stale entries against current evidence before assignment. Do not invent work, reopen verified results without cause, or browse unrelated history. Recheck tasks deferred for collisions whenever their dependency or file ownership clears.

heading: Keep actionable work assigned
text: Reuse context only when it remains trustworthy: verify its provenance, current files or hashes, branch, assumptions, and unresolved decisions. Fresh assignments should carry settled decisions and relevant evidence without stale conversation baggage. If a worker's context degrades, obtain a diary and verify the handoff against actual state before transferring ownership. Retire that worker only after the receiving owner has enough verified context; do not abandon its unfinished work.

heading: Blockers, checkpoints, and completion
text: A task is complete only when its acceptance criteria are verified and the shared task list is updated with evidence and any limitations. Then reversibly archive its completed thread after preserving its handoff and confirming no operation or unfinished assignment remains. Keep unfinished and pending threads open. Do not confuse archiving a thread with deleting a branch, worktree, or files.

heading: Blockers, checkpoints, and completion
text: Continue the sprint until `STOP SPRINT` or a genuinely confirmed account usage reset. An announced reset ETA, estimated timer, expected replenishment, or unknown reset state is not confirmation. Verify a reset through authoritative account usage evidence; unknown means unknown. If execution becomes unavailable, record the interruption and pending state rather than claiming a reset or a safe stop.

heading: Stop at a safe boundary
text: The parent summarizes completed work, diaries still in progress, parked or unassigned tasks, unresolved work, and any running or unknown operations. Update the register, preserve unfinished threads, and release ownership only when safe. Claim **safely stopped** only after verifying all relevant operations and handoffs; otherwise state precisely what is still running or unverified. A later sprint requires a new user activation.

text: Stop acknowledged: “⚠️ Stop received. New work is halted; active owners are reaching safe boundaries and writing handoffs. [Operation] remains running, so safe stop is not yet verified.”

heading: Distinct quantities and one inclusion contract
text: For rest-of-week **pregame** totals, include only future, not-yet-started games with a validated start timestamp and eligible schedule state at `asOf`. Keep started, completed, cancelled and postponed/unscheduled games visible as status context but exclude them from future means. heading: Retained release contract
text: The retained source clamps finite odds to 0–100 and keeps null/nonfinite odds neutral using the total included-game denominator. UI must still show missing odds/coverage; a neutral computational fallback is not observed 50% probability. Preserve the old `-100` no-games sentinel at compatibility boundaries if required, but model it internally as `status=no_games`, never a poor forecast. If the active league changes, use verified `2L/T`; do not describe 16 as the number of fantasy teams.

heading: Retained release contract
text: The retained source's equal-schedule numerical guarantee is monotonicity in its supplied win-odds input; it does **not** establish the stronger semantic claim that actual easier scoring opponents always rank higher. Keep that distinction in release copy. The category-environment replacement below must satisfy the scoring-ease property when the evidence is aligned and comparable; missing evidence cannot fulfill that property through invention.

heading: Illustrative slate grade, not a fitted probability
text: **Horizon-independent proof.** Let each compared team have any finite nonempty included game set after date/type/status/exclusion filtering. Complete valid slate inputs imply `0≤q≤1`; therefore their averages imply `-1≤C≤1`. If a grade cannot be applied because scope is incomplete, use applied grade 0 with a missingness label, also within the bound. Let both teams share the same selected league context `(L,T)` and score version. Subtracting their scores cancels `-6×2L/T`, giving `ΔS1 = 6ΔGP + 4ΔON + ΔM + εΔC`. Since `ΔM≥-1` and `εΔC≥-0.5`, the lower bounds are 6.5 for `(ΔGP,ΔON)=(0,2)`, 0.5 for `(1,-1)`, and 2.5 for `(0,1)`. The proof holds for **every finite supported 7/10/custom horizon and every common exclusion state**, not just the reference examples. It also covers missing matchup inputs, whose neutral contribution remains bounded. An exclusion state that removes all games yields the no-games state; a requested GP/ON comparison no longer applies to a team without those GP/ON counts. Different horizons, different team-specific league centering, per-target rescaling or score versions cannot use this guarantee.

heading: Illustrative slate grade, not a fitted probability
text: Retaining the GP/ON guarantees intentionally prioritizes the owner's simple schedule-ordering policy over allowing a more realistic crowding model to reorder those cases. A personalized legal-start score may validly reverse these rankings, but must be separately named and evaluated. If the owner prefers realistic population/roster startability to dominate the generic ranking, D1 must change explicitly rather than hide that choice in coefficients.

heading: Score explanation and examples
text: The displayed components are rounded; compute/sort on full precision and offer exact values in detail. An unavailable component must say unavailable/neutral fallback, not imply a measured zero. Example retained reference: four games, three ON, `L=47`, odds `[60,60,60,null]` gives `M≈0.075` and `S0≈18.450` (the retained JavaScript formatter returns 18.4 for this value). heading: Category-specific SoS and opponent environment
text: Proposed research baseline: estimate opponent category allowed rates from deduplicated, strength-state-specific prior games, with exposure-aware denominators and shrinkage toward a same-season prior. Use recency weights chosen with rolling validation; effective exposure/sample size must follow those weights. Model source/venue scorer effects only where historical evidence supports them. Estimate home/away, pace, rest, goalie/lineup information and PP/PK components once. If unavailable, omit the effect or use an explicitly labeled approved prior; never substitute zero.

heading: Category-specific SoS and opponent environment
text: For a scoring category `c`, estimate an opponent factor `m(o,c)=neutral-team expected category versus opponent / neutral-team expected category versus league-average opponent`, holding focal ability, exposure and credit definition fixed. A candidate bounded score term is `0.5 × mean(tanh(log(m(o,c))/s_c))`, with finite positive factor/denominator and scale `s_c>0` fixed from training data only. Reject unsupported/nonfinite factors rather than silently invent a floor. Unknown factors contribute neutral to the score but stay missing in the evidence/coverage record; divide score contribution by all included games. A comparable known easier scoring factor increases the term; finite-input monotonicity and bounds must be tested. This is a proposed calibrated environment input, not permission to use unqualified allowed-rate ratios as a forecast.

heading: Team/player forecast reconciliation
text: An additive weekly team category mean is the sum of admitted per-game means for exactly the included future games. Do not sum per-game quantiles to form an interval. A weekly variance needs `sum variances + 2 sum covariances`; aggregate simulation needs an approved dependence model. Without that, provide means and per-game uncertainty or an explicitly qualified independent-game approximation that passed validation. A team-metric confidence band, a predictive outcome interval and uncertain forecast inputs must be named separately.

heading: A. Fix the population before improving the algorithm
text: Avoid multiplying participation twice when an existing minutes forecast already includes nonappearances. Goalie-start labels must come from official starts or verified start-of-game evidence, not whichever goalie played the most minutes.

heading: B. Separate opportunity error from ability error
text: The appearance-probability identity above is exact when a nonappearance contributes zero. Within its conditional term, multiplying expected minutes by an expected production rate is only an approximation when minutes and rates vary together; label that approximation. PP1/PP2/no-PP scenarios give a tractable way to carry joint role uncertainty without pretending the future role is certain. Forecast team PP opportunity separately from player deployment: a zero-PP-minute game does not by itself prove the player lost their role. PP clock-time shares across skaters do not sum to one; use explicit manpower-aware skater-minute budgets. EV must not silently mean only 5v5, and extra-attacker play must not automatically become an official power play.

heading: D. Improve shrinkage and adaptation without daily winner chasing
text: Test one time-adaptive alternative against a static/shrunk baseline: recency-weighted rates first; a state-space rate model later if residuals show a remaining adaptation problem. Separate latent ability from role changes. A trade should not automatically erase talent history, but it may reset or change workload/context expectations.

heading: G. Compare methods on the right score
text: Selection itself can overfit a noisy validation score; the general risk is documented by Cawley and Talbot. Use chronological inner development for choices and later outer periods for evaluating the chosen procedure. [S6] Do not invent a minimum sample size, fixed 1% improvement gate or standard-error percentage. Set a practically meaningful gain and uncertainty plan before the next experiment. With too few independent dates, report inconclusive rather than a precise confidence claim. Dependence can arise within game/date and across repeated players; the inference design must account for it. [S7]

heading: I. Require shot-quality sophistication to prove its forecasting value
text: Compare direct goals rates against shot-volume × finishing, then add native predicted shot mix only if it earns a gain. An xG model trained on unblocked attempts does not directly supply a goal probability per SOG; denominators must match. Separate G, primary/secondary A and PP contributions only when labels support them. Retain an “other players” residual when reconciling team totals; the pilot subset must not receive every team goal or shot. Evaluate any reconciliation or clipping as part of the final predictor.

heading: 1. Introduction and overview
text: The Roster Schedule Optimizer (RSO) helps an in-season fantasy hockey manager turn a limited acquisition budget into useful, legal starting contributions during a matchup or custom date range. It combines roster-slot scheduling, candidate comparisons, goalie-minimum planning and a sequence of proposed moves. A recommendation must improve the manager's feasible lineup; adding scheduled NHL games alone does not establish a gain.

heading: 1. Introduction and overview
text: FORGE supplies qualified player and goalie forecasts. RSO uses them to evaluate roster decisions, and Start Chart provides consistent daily comparisons. Comparable forecasts must match player/game identity, horizon, cutoff and lineage. Team-goal research alone cannot supply the individual category contributions required by RSO, and acceptance of a separate team-goals model is not an RSO prerequisite.

heading: 1. Introduction and overview
text: The first controlled daily-lineup beta must include both free/manual and premium/Yahoo-connected users. It requires positive compatible real-data player/goalie consumption plus engineering and data-integrity acceptance. TJ's subsequent P3 decision permits a controlled beta with clear evaluation limitations while quality evidence accumulates; the initial evaluation sample is not a universal beta gate. Broader performance claims and model-weight changes need stronger untouched evidence. Weekly-lock support and the completed commercial lifecycle are additional full-launch requirements.

heading: 2. Goals
text: 2. Compare maximum legal starts with best supported projected outcome against the same optimized no-acquisition baseline. Every claimed gain must account for displaced starts and contributions.

heading: 3. User stories
text: - As a category manager, I want to see banked results, remaining opportunities and category tradeoffs so I can pursue attainable categories and avoid wasteful moves.

heading: FR1. Planning context and setup
text: The system must support matchup weeks, inclusive custom date ranges and midweek planning. Identify the season, provider, league, team, league timezone, selected dates and evidence time. Manual setup must support player search/paste, canonical identity resolution, unresolved names, actual slots, scoring and acquisition rules, with local progress retained.

heading: FR1. Planning context and setup
text: Use authoritative league boundaries and distinguish acquisition resets from lineup locks. Charge an acquisition to its submission period and evaluate contributions from its effective time, including a legal Sunday submission effective Monday. Do not treat a current-week counter as verified future-week allowance. Optional opponent/scoreboard inputs must not require reconstruction of every league roster for useful schedule planning.

heading: FR4. Baseline, marginal gains and explanations
text: Scheduled GP alone must not determine value. Recommend no acquisition when no defensible improvement exists. Label bounded-search results as “best found” and disclose their limits; do not claim a global optimum.

heading: FR5. Timed streaming sequences
text: Spend up to the remaining allowance; do not assume the full allowance must be spent. Distinguish the next actionable move from conditional later moves. Preserve a valid sequence prefix if a conditional suffix fails. Future candidate availability is not guaranteed.

heading: FR6. Candidate availability and rule authority
text: Separate executable free-agent paths, conditional waiver paths, exclusions and unknown availability. Current league evidence or explicit manager verification must establish addability. Public catalog membership, low ownership and absence from the user's roster do not establish availability.

heading: FR6. Candidate availability and rule authority
text: Identify provider-verified rules, manager inputs/overrides and unknowns with their sources and observation times. Unknown rules or availability must block dependent actionable conclusions or be visible scenario assumptions. Retained/manual evidence must remain visibly unverified when current provider verification is unavailable.

heading: FR7. Ranked candidate alternatives
text: Provide **By Team** and **All Players** views, retaining the existing `candidateByTeam` / `AllPlayers` roles. Within displayed team/position groups, rank by usable model-projected points when supported. All Players must consider both actual AGP and projected points/outcome, with team and position filters; no fixed blend is approved.

heading: FR7. Ranked candidate alternatives
text: Default to ten displayed alternatives, with five/ten/twenty choices. Use clear eligibility and availability headings, retain full legal eligibility and distinguish unknown from verified availability. Unsupported projected rankings must be labelled unavailable rather than filled with plausible values.

heading: FR8. Responsible drops and supporting context
text: Evaluate expendability using low active-game contribution together with low projected contribution. Ownership may be a fallback signal, but does not justify dropping a strong player. Respect the manager's protected list and never silently replace selected moves. Any automatic must-keep threshold remains a proposal.

heading: FR9. Category and matchup decisions
text: Use league-specific points scoring, supported category utility or supported matchup-win analysis. Incorporate banked results and remaining opportunity; explain categories within reach and categories that may reasonably be faded. Missing categories must remain explicit.

heading: FR10. Goalie minimum planning
text: Consider remaining actionable dates and back-to-backs without presuming a backup rotation or counting competing goalies as two starts for one team-game. Explain ratio risk from extra starts after the minimum is met.

heading: FR11. Goalie evidence labels
text: Distinguish confirmed, expected/projected, unknown, disputed and stale evidence. Bind each confirmation to the correct player, team and game, with source time, authority, corrections and expiry. A probability threshold or assumed back-to-back split must not create a confirmed start.

heading: FR12. Workspace continuity and manager intent
text: Preserve selections, preferences, unresolved imports, exclusions, protections and explicit active/bench locks. Allow temporary objective comparisons. Refresh, undo, reopening and context/account switching must preserve manager intent while retaining correct current provider authority. Proposed repairs must be reviewable and must not silently replace selected moves.

heading: FR12. Workspace continuity and manager intent
text: Account saves must isolate owners and use optimistic concurrency: a save based on an older version must not overwrite a newer saved plan without conflict handling. Ignore late responses belonging to another context or account.

heading: FR14. Honest degraded states
text: Distinguish fresh, stale, partial, fallback and unavailable states. Preserve saved workspaces when planning or access endpoints fail. Missing forecasts, unsupported categories, unverified eligibility and unverified participation must not become reassuring zeros, certainty or populated fixtures.

heading: FR14. Honest degraded states
text: Keep supported schedule analysis available with explicit limitations. Do not display a complete available-player list or full projected comparison when the required coverage is incomplete.

heading: FR15. Shared forecast contract and acceptance
text: RSO and Start Chart must consume compatible player-level forecasts with matching games, horizons, cutoffs and model/source lineage for comparable outputs. Admission must establish canonical identity, cutoff-known inputs, supported categories/estimators, participation/exposure, coverage and provenance. Zero forecast rows or team-goal research alone do not satisfy acceptance.

heading: FR15. Shared forecast contract and acceptance
text: Separate conditional performance from appearance-weighted contribution. Require supported full-game scope and named residual contributors when reconciliation needs them. Reconcile matching scope/lineage; do not mechanically distribute team goals into player projections. Preserve original forecast revisions and evaluate later revisions separately. Apply the input-specific freshness warnings and declared-comparison coverage in P1–P2. Numerical quality thresholds and remaining evaluation details require review under section 9.

Retain eventual nonparticipants, missing forecasts, cancelled/rescheduled games and unresolved outcomes with explicit statuses; an absent outcome or projection is never a zero. Use the accepted first 14-slate/500-skater-player-game/100-goalie-start milestone for diagnostic reporting. Propose the **following 28 chronological slates**, reaching **1,000 skater player-games and 200 goalie starts**, as a larger untouched evaluation reference. Do not inspect its outcomes while selecting models/metrics. These larger numbers are proposals, not sufficient evidence by themselves or beta gates. Freeze exact dates and counting rules after an authorized issuance path exists, before outcomes become known. Held-out forecast errors must use later observations rather than fitting residuals. [Forecasting: Principles and Practice](https://otexts.com/fpp3/accuracy.html).

heading: Forecast freshness, coverage and numerical acceptance
text: - **Cutoff-safe baseline:** Prefer the existing admitted player/goalie rate baseline when available, with its exact algorithm and input snapshot frozen before outcomes. Match player/game, horizon, cutoff, membership and target semantics. Use only supported participation/exposure, applying it once according to the declared basis; never substitute team-goal research for player forecasts. A later baseline replay must be labelled as a replay from frozen inputs, and cannot stand in for the genuinely pregame-issued model forecast. Missing baseline heads remain coverage gaps and cannot support a paired skill claim.

heading: Forecast freshness, coverage and numerical acceptance
text: - **Category-specific checks:** For published mean forecasts, propose **mean squared error** as the primary score; report mean absolute error and signed bias as diagnostics in each category's native units. Select a matching score first if a forecast declares a different estimand. Evaluate ratio numerator/denominator components separately and recompute full-horizon ratios only with known positive exposure; retain undefined ratios. Do not average unlike category errors into an overall accuracy grade. Squared and absolute error target different point forecasts, so the score must match the forecast's stated target. [Making and Evaluating Point Forecasts](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0912.0902).

heading: Category comparisons and protection
text: **P4 — Category utility and comparison display (direction confirmed; equivalence tolerance open).** Use actual startable plan outcomes under the league's scoring and the same horizon/baseline. Show supported per-category gains/losses and alternatives without an automatic blend. **5%** is approved only as a clearly labelled provisional **“similar projected points”** display rule, never a confidence interval or automatic decision threshold. Its denominator is the larger absolute supported plan total; normalize each total by that denominator before taking their difference to avoid subtraction/division overflow or underflow. Two known zero totals are equal; missing/nonfinite totals are not comparable, and signed totals retain their signs. Display the absolute point difference as well so tiny totals do not imply a meaningful gain. Prefer fewer acquisitions only when supported outcomes are otherwise equivalent under a separately declared numerical tolerance. That tolerance remains open; show gain and acquisition cost for meaningful tradeoffs. Category weights and inferred must-keep rules require separate approval.

heading: Category comparisons and protection
text: **P5 — Drop protection (direction confirmed).** Keep automatic must-keep protection **off** and respect explicit manager protections. Check legal vacant slots and IR/IR+ capacity before recommending a drop, and preserve manager-selected moves. Drop protection and lineup locks remain separate constraints. Category weights or inferred must-keep rules need a separate approved policy; ownership alone must not become drop permission.

heading: Performance, refresh and workload
text: **P6 — Latency and bounded search.** Propose **p95 ≤2 seconds** for optimized no-acquisition calculation and **p95 ≤5 seconds** for a proposed streaming plan, measured from calculation request to usable result. Start evaluation with 19/20/25-player rosters, 7- and 14-day horizons, up to 250 verified candidate records and a four-acquisition limit. Propose a **20-second search ceiling** that returns a valid best-found result or an explicit incomplete/unavailable result while preserving the workspace. This is a declared test workload, not a production candidate cap or permission to shorten horizons. Measure genuine workload distributions before approval.

text: **P9 — Price.** Propose **$9.99 for one seasonal purchase** as an owner-review pricing hypothesis. No market validation, revenue forecast or agreement is implied, and the historical $5.99 Draft Pro price remains separate. TJ must approve price and what the package includes before commercial implementation.

heading: Seasonal access, pricing and entitlement edges
text: **P11 — Time boundaries.** Propose **America/New_York** for commercial access. End season access at **July 1, 2027, 00:00**, making June 30 inclusive. Start the common preview at **00:00 on an owner-declared season-opening date**, ending exactly 14 days later; a late purchaser receives the remainder of the common window. It must preserve every source event for audit while presenting and writing the earliest valid source for a team/date/game/signal bucket.

heading: Introduction/Overview
text: The generic raw-event, receiver, parser, snapshot, first-arrival display, canonical `lineCombinations`, parser-coverage, roster-move, and bounded-backfill foundations are implemented. The authoritative schema/provenance rollout and a Gamecenter consumer probe are production-verified. Remaining work is the explicit production/provider checkpoint: unresolved-name email proof, three IFTTT applets, and one controlled event per account through the bounded end-to-end evidence flow.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 1. The system must support `GameDayGoalies`, `GameDayLines`, and `GameDayNewsNHL` as distinct configured sources in the `gdl_suite` source group.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 2. Each IFTTT receiver must validate its configured secret, deduplicate by stable event/tweet identity, persist the raw event before optional processing, and retain the full payload plus received/updated timestamps.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 3. Raw events must preserve source group/key/account, username, tweet text, tweet URL and ID, creation labels/timestamps, processing state, and raw payload.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 4. The generic processor must support one source account, all GDL accounts, or all configured sources without duplicating shared CCC/GDT parsing logic.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 5. Processing must reuse tweet-ID/URL normalization, oEmbed caching/backoff, quoted-post resolution, classification, NHL filtering, roster matching, unresolved-name queueing, rejected-row persistence, and event-status updates.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 6. Source hints may upgrade otherwise-`other` rows conservatively for goalie, lineup/practice, or injury/transaction language, but must not override an explicit parser classification; applied hints must be recorded in metadata.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 7. Accepted and rejected snapshots must retain source group/key/account at the top level and in metadata, and capture keys must avoid cross-source collisions.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 8. First-arrival buckets must use snapshot date, resolved team, game when known, normalized signal type, and subtype where necessary.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 9. Initial normalized signal types must cover `lineup`, `goalie_start`, `injury`, `practice_lines`, and `power_play`, with explicit roster-move subtypes added only when evidence supports them.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 10. Only accepted observed rows may win a display or downstream bucket. Rejected and ambiguous rows must remain queryable but must not drive user-facing selection or `lineCombinations` writes.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 11. Winner ordering must use exact tweet-posted time when available, fall back to received/observed time when necessary, and break ties deterministically by source key, tweet ID, and capture key.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 12. `/twitterEmbeds` must load accepted rows from every configured tweet-line source, group them by the canonical bucket, render the first-arrival winner, show its source label, preserve auto-refresh, and retain access to non-winning source evidence.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 13. The system must define a single reusable first-arrival helper/contract shared by `/twitterEmbeds` and `lineCombinations` updates so selection cannot drift between display and persistence.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 14. Before writing tweet-derived data, the implementation must verify the canonical `lineCombinations` array fields, game/team identity semantics, provenance behavior, writers, and consumers. The stale snake-case `line_combinations` table is historical evidence, not the active downstream contract.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 15. `lineCombinations` writes may use accepted lineup/practice-line rows and explicitly supported high-confidence goalie-only updates. Lower-confidence injury/transaction signals must remain metadata or domain-specific records unless a downstream contract is approved.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 16. A winning snapshot must map into the existing flattened player-ID arrays (`forwards`, `defensemen`, `goalies`) keyed by `gameId` and `teamId`, with additive provenance fields that do not break existing readers.

heading: Functional Requirements

heading: Functional Requirements

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 21. Supported roster-move handling must cover high-confidence call-up, assignment/sent-down, healthy-scratch/removal, trade, waiver, signing, activation, return, and IR language while keeping uncertain signals in metadata.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 22. Player names in roster-move signals must be cross-referenced against canonical roster/player data; unresolved names must remain explicit.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 23. The processor must offer production-safe bounded catch-up parameters for pending configured sources by date and must paginate Supabase/PostgREST reads until a short page when result sets can exceed the page cap.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 24. `process=true` must never prevent the raw event from being stored when oEmbed fetching, parsing, or downstream persistence fails; processing failures must remain retryable and observable.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 25. Operator documentation must include IFTTT configuration, pending/accepted/rejected/winner queries, `lineCombinations` verification, retry/backfill behavior, and the cron safety-net recommendation.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 28. The external IFTTT receiver must never return or log a raw downstream processor response body or exception message; failed `process=true` follow-up may expose only a stable error classification and bounded HTTP status while leaving the raw event retryable.

heading: Functional Requirements

heading: Introduction/Overview
text: Natural Stat Trick has changed the supported path for automated access as of April 2026. Scrapers and bots are expected to use `data.naturalstattrick.com` instead of `www.naturalstattrick.com`, and every request must include an approved access key either as the `nst-key` header or as a `key` query parameter. The main site is being hardened against scraper traffic before the 2026 playoffs, so the current FHFH NST integrations are at risk of partial failure or full breakage if they continue to call the legacy host.

heading: Introduction/Overview
text: This project will audit every direct NST caller in the repository, migrate them to the supported data subdomain and key-based authentication flow, and validate that each migrated endpoint produces the same downstream behavior as the current scripts. The work must also replace the old NST rate-limit assumptions with the new token-based operating model, add environment-based key management for local and deployed server environments, and produce an operator-facing rollout and monitoring runbook.

heading: 1. Introduction / Overview
text: This project replaces the repo's NST-scraped game-level skater and goalie metrics with an NHL public API ingestion and derivation pipeline. The new system must preserve the current product's useful strength-split metrics, prefer NHL-derived correctness when it conflicts with NST edge-case behavior, and create a scalable data foundation for later xG model training from normalized play-by-play and shift data.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 1. The system must ingest NHL public API data from `play-by-play`, `landing`, `boxscore`, and `shiftcharts` endpoints for a target game or batch of games.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 2. The system must store immutable raw payload snapshots with endpoint metadata, fetch timestamps, and content hashes to support replay and auditability.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 3. The system must normalize `play-by-play` payloads into one event row per event, preserving both typed columns and raw `details` JSON.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 4. The system must normalize `shiftcharts` payloads into one shift row per shift record rather than storing only per-player aggregates.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 5. The system must normalize `play-by-play.rosterSpots` into a reusable game-roster table.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 6. The system must decode `situationCode` using the empirically validated order `awayGoalie, awaySkaters, homeSkaters, homeGoalie`.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 7. The system must store both exact manpower labels such as `5v5`, `5v4`, `6v5`, and `3v3` and canonical strength states such as `EV`, `PP`, `SH`, and `EN`.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 8. The system must treat NHL-derived correctness as the source of truth when it conflicts with NST edge-case behavior, and any intentional divergence must be documented and versioned.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 9. The system must reconstruct skater and goalie metric families currently relied on from NST-era tables, including all-situations, even-strength, power-play, and penalty-kill splits.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 10. The system must support individual counts, on-ice counts, rates, on-ice rates, zone starts, zone faceoffs, and related strength-aware outputs where they are currently part of the repo’s NST contract.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 11. The system must exclude shootout events from NST-style skater and goalie parity metrics.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 12. The system must treat empty-net states separately from true goalie-in-net EV, PP, and SH states.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 13. The system must derive on-ice attribution from raw shift rows rather than inferring on-ice state only from event ownership.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 14. The system must support phase 1 derived classifications for rush, rebound, flurry, and danger buckets.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 15. The system must support normalized attacking-direction coordinates for downstream distance and angle calculations.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 16. The system must support prior-event context features such as previous event type, previous event team, time since prior event, and distance from prior event.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 17. The system must support query-parameter-driven historical backfill while defaulting operational flows to current-season updates.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 18. The system must be idempotent for replaying the same game ingest multiple times without creating duplicate logical records.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 19. The system must expose reusable library modules for raw ingest, event parsing, strength decoding, shift stint reconstruction, derived feature generation, parity generation, and validation.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 20. The system must include route- or job-level entry points that fit existing repo audit and auth patterns for one game, a date range, and backfill mode.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 21. The system must validate normalized event totals against raw payload totals for every ingested game.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 22. The system must validate parity outputs against representative existing NST-era outputs for sampled games, teams, players, and goalies.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 23. The system must version parser logic, feature logic, and parity logic so future behavior changes are replayable and attributable.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements
text: 24. The system must keep model-input tables separate from parity-output tables and separate both from raw upstream storage.

heading: 4. Functional Requirements

text: The PRD pairs two existing source lists: `tasks-xg-release-remediation.md` and `tasks-xg-release-exception-resolution.md`. The resolved contract must keep raw mismatches visible while separating true blockers from approved exceptions; it must never force a pass or hide disagreement.

text: Goaltending is the NHL’s highest-variance role: traditional outcomes (GAA, Sv%) are heavily polluted by team context and random event variance, and even “better” metrics (GSAx) show weak year-over-year repeatability. heading: Forecasting and feature engineering
text: **Resource 9. Christian Lee’s Random Forest article.** The useful part here is not the reported ~70% accuracy by itself; it is the author’s own recognition that some strong features are likely informative because they contain current-game goal information. The article flags that metrics like same-game 5v5 save percentage can inflate accuracy, and its stated next step is to remove goal-containing features and rely only on prior information—exactly the right leakage discipline for FORGE. citeturn22view3turn22view4

heading: What the resources imply for FORGE
text: For `run-projection-accuracy.ts`, `accuracy.ts`, and the metadata returned by `goalies.ts`, the resources strongly support **grading probabilities, not just picks**. Several of the sources work in log loss, Brier score, cross-validation splits, and calibration thinking. Your existing mention of calibration snapshots is exactly the right direction. The next step is to make those diagnostics more granular: by position, by stat type, by confidence bucket, by starter-certainty bucket, by early/mid/late season, and by whether the eventual starter matched the model prior. citeturn6view1turn10view0turn12view2turn13view1turn22view3

heading: Where the biggest gaps are
text: - **Consistency should be operationalized carefully, not romanticized.** Team-level consistency is probably lower leverage than average performance, while player-level consistency is more useful when attached to metric stickiness and sample-size-aware uncertainty. If FORGE does not yet distinguish those cases, it risks displaying “trend” or “consistency” in a way that overstates signal. citeturn18view1turn2view0turn25view1

heading: Where the biggest gaps are
text: - **Calibration coverage should be broader than “overall accuracy.”** Good public models expose log loss, Brier score, calibration, and often confidence-conditioned performance. If FORGE does not yet score itself by confidence bucket, starter-certainty bucket, stat type, and season segment, you know less than you think about where the model is actually strong. citeturn6view1turn10view0turn12view2turn13view1

heading: 1. Introduction / Overview
text: The platform should use the NHL public API plus the statistics already available in the existing Supabase database. The first production version should prioritize a reliable game prediction pipeline, a detailed public analytics page, and a measurable model feedback loop. Player and goalie predictions are in scope, but they should be implemented in a lightweight, non-blocking way at first. The game prediction model must still work when player-level or confirmed goalie data is incomplete.

heading: Schema-aligned direction
text: Do not use latest-only display views, such as `nhl_team_data`, as historical training inputs. Historical feature generation must join dated source rows as-of the prediction timestamp.

heading: Schema-aligned direction
text: Representative row-level checks passed for schedule required fields and duplicate natural keys across the primary planned sources. Remaining quality work is filtering or clipping recent WGO/goalie outliers, excluding or classifying non-one-game NST gamelog rows, and handling the 56 audited 2025-10-01+ game/team sides that do not have a recent team-power or standings row within the 14-day lookback used by the audit.

heading: Schema-aligned direction
text: As-of/leakage checks confirm that historical training must use stricter cutoffs than current display logic. `nhl_team_data` exists but is not a planned training source and should stay excluded. Team features should prefer rows dated before the game date; the audit found 88 game/team sides missing pregame `team_power_ratings_daily`/WGO rows and 32 sides where team power was same-day-only. Most current `goalie_start_projections` rows were created after scheduled puck drop, so they are useful for current predictions but not historical training unless a pregame snapshot/backfill is created. `lineCombinations` lacks an observation timestamp, some line-source rows are observed after start time, and FORGE projections use date-level `as_of_date` values that are usually on or after game date; all of these must be optional or conservatively excluded from historical training until pregame-safe provenance exists.

heading: Schema-aligned direction
text: For standings, record/split math passed, but field names are not always scale-safe. In particular, `nhl_standings_details.goals_for_pctg` and `goal_differential_pctg` behave as rate-like fields in live data and must be documented in the feature dictionary before normalization.

heading: Schema-aligned direction
text: Goalie-source audit results also shape v1. `goalie_start_projections` has full schedule-side coverage in its current date range, so it remains the primary starter-probability source, but the model must normalize or flag game/team groups whose probabilities do not sum to roughly 1 and review extreme `projected_gsaa_per_60` values. Recent `wgo_goalie_stats` rows behave as goalie-game rows; `wgo_goalie_stats_totals` is not historical-training-safe without a snapshot/as-of rule. NST goalie sources include all, 5v5, EV, PP, and PK count/rate tables, but they currently top out at 2026-04-09 and rate fields need low-TOI outlier handling before training.

heading: Schema-aligned direction
text: Lineup/player-context audit confirms these sources must remain optional in v1. `lineCombinations` is mostly populated for the audited current-season window but still misses 50 game/team sides. `lines_nhl`, `lines_dfo`, `lines_gdl`, and `lines_ccc` are sparse prospective sources rather than full historical training inputs. FORGE player/goalie/team projections are useful optional context only when fresh, and `forge_roster_events` should not be required while the table is empty.

text: | Goalie starts | `goalie_start_projections` | Starter probability, confirmation state, projected goalie quality | Required for current predictions, not safe for historical training without snapshots | Current predictions may use latest fresh rows; backtests need rows created before puck drop or a pregame backfill | Blend likely starters; fall back to team goalie strength | Go current-only; training blocked until backfilled |

text: The live source audit adds one important qualification: the NST gamelog tables are the preferred rolling-window inputs, while `nst_team_5v5`, `nst_team_all`, `nst_team_pp`, and `nst_team_pk` should be treated as cumulative/snapshot tables. heading: Repository schema alignment and corrected direction
text: The row-level quality pass found no required-field issues in recent schedule rows and no duplicate natural-key groups in representative planned sources. The remaining row-level concerns are operational rather than schema-blocking: recent WGO/goalie outliers need clipping or review, NST gamelog rows with `gp <> 1` must be excluded or classified before rolling-window use, and a small set of recent game/team sides lacks team-power or standings context inside the audit's 14-day lookback.

heading: Repository schema alignment and corrected direction
text: The storage audit narrows this further. The existing prediction output tables are empty and payload-complete, which is good for first public serving rows, but they do not include a prediction ID, `computed_at` in the primary key, `feature_snapshot_id`, or `run_id`. `forge_runs` is useful as shared run metadata, but not enough by itself for game-model evaluation slices unless metrics are written with explicit model/version/feature-set/date-segment keys. `source_provenance_snapshots` should be reused where practical, but current null/expired freshness rows mean the prediction pipeline must write its own source cutoffs and fallback flags into prediction history or feature snapshots.

heading: Repository schema alignment and corrected direction
text: One important leakage correction follows from the schema: avoid using "latest-only" views such as `nhl_team_data` for historical training rows. They can be useful for current UI display, but historical features must be recreated from dated tables with `date < game.startTime::date` or a stricter prediction timestamp cutoff. Similarly, season-to-date tables and rolling views must be joined as-of the prediction time, not as-of the current database state.

heading: Source-by-source analysis
text: **entity["people","Gianni Pischedda","sports modeling author"].** Pischedda’s 2014 follow-up is useful less for the specific model and more for the criticism it makes of hockey feature folklore. Using the Ottawa dataset, it argues that simple contextual variables like Team and Location drove much of the predictive power while many complex derived metrics added less than people assumed, and it proposed a day-by-day dynamic model-building framework for practical prediction. I would not elevate its exact results into “truth,” because it relies partly on proprietary tooling and an inherited dataset, but its directional insight matters: context variables and sequential updating can matter as much as increasingly elaborate hockey-specific aggregates. citeturn27view0turn28view0turn28view1

heading: Source-by-source analysis
text: **Skytte on xG model design.** His 2025 xG 2.0 article adds a newer layer: running three-year models tested on the following season instead of a single random train/test split. It reports that XGBoost outperformed logistic regression, random forest was weak in his implementation, BoxID shot location plus handedness was by far the dominant feature, and removing the rebound variable improved predictiveness for future results even if rebound information can help describe current shot danger. For you, the key takeaway is not “must use XGBoost,” but rather that shot-location model design, temporal testing, and feature pruning matter more than piling on more event annotations. citeturn38view0turn38view2

heading: Source-by-source analysis
text: **entity["people","Christian Lee","hockey stats writer"].** The random-forest Medium article is best read as a cautionary source. It reports roughly 70% accuracy and names Net.PP, Net.PK, blocks, and offensive-versus-defensive-zone faceoff differential among the most important features. But the article also openly acknowledges that statistics like same-game even-strength save percentage can contain goal information from the game itself and therefore inflate apparent predictive accuracy. The author says future work should use prior information only. That makes this source extremely useful for identifying leak-prone features and for understanding why impressive raw accuracies can be misleading in pregame sports models. citeturn19view4turn19view2

heading: Overlapping methods, differing methods, strong methods, and sub-optimal methods
text: The biggest disagreements are about horizon and granularity. Older long-horizon work and xG literature argue that xG and Corsi are better than goals for predicting future scoring over many games, while Skytte’s one-game-ahead tests find that actual goals can be as good or better than xG in a micro-prediction setting. Likewise, some sources push player-based lineup models, but Skytte’s own follow-up found that using player-level on-ice stats did not clearly outperform team-based versions when the model was otherwise built on on-ice metrics. The practical inference is that a next-game website model should absolutely include xG, but it should not be embarrassed to use rolling goal differential too, and it should begin team-plus-goalie first unless player-level incremental lift is proven. citeturn12search0turn36search0turn11view4

heading: Which statistics appear most important
text: Third, treat **goaltending and likely starter identity** as non-negotiable. MoneyPuck gives goaltending 29% of model influence, Blackport includes starter WAR, starter Game Score, and goals-saved terms, and Schwaeber explicitly makes the goalie the lone exception to a top-down team model because the starter/backup gap matters. The strongest practical form is not generic team save percentage; it is starter-specific recent and multi-season quality, ideally blended with a starting-goalie probability model when confirmation is not yet public. citeturn24view1turn24view3turn39view3turn6search0

heading: Open questions and limitations
text: The most important unresolved design choice for your build is not the algorithm. It is whether you want v1 to be a lean pregame win-probability model or a broader ecosystem that also predicts player and goalie performance and then rolls those estimates upward. The source base supports starting lean. The player-first path can be more expressive, but it is more expensive and public evidence does not yet show that it is clearly better than a well-built team-plus-goalie model for next-game prediction. citeturn6search0turn12search0turn17view0

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `players`: contributes the player processing universe and player search data; metric families depending on it are all rolling families indirectly and all debug selectors directly; classification is authoritative for player identity and scope; quirks are none beyond goalie exclusion rules in batch processing; freshness dependency is normal roster freshness; known refresh path is not in the inspected rolling file surface and must be recorded in the runbook from the current operational player ingest workflow.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `games`: contributes chronological game ordering, team schedule ledger, known `game_id` validation, and current-team rolling availability denominators; metric families depending on it are availability / participation and all row identity scopes; classification is authoritative; quirks are team-game chronology and team-stint alignment; freshness dependency is critical because stale `games` corrupts availability windows and unknown-game diagnostics; refresh path is not in the inspected rolling file surface and must be captured from the current game ingest workflow before audit execution.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `wgo_skater_stats`: contributes the row spine, appearance dates, original `game_id`, team abbreviation, WGO fallback counts, WGO PP share fallback inputs, and WGO TOI fallback inputs; metric families depending on it are all families through row existence plus additive fallback, PP share fallback, and TOI fallback; classification is authoritative for row spine and fallback for a narrow stat subset; quirks are `toi_per_game` may be minutes or seconds and `pp_toi_pct_per_game` is share-like but fallback-only; freshness dependency is critical because every rolling row is WGO-anchored; no writer was found in the inspected surface, so the runbook must document the exact current WGO refresh job or endpoint from operations.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_as_counts`: contributes all-strength player raw counts such as goals, assists, points, shots, ixG, iSCF, iHDCF, hits, blocks, and penalties drawn; metric families depending on it are surface counting stats, weighted `/60`, finishing, expected / chance, and some ratio numerators; classification is authoritative; quirks are raw counts should outrank WGO fallback values; freshness dependency is critical for all-strength validation; no writer was found in the inspected surface, so the runbook must document the current NST counts refresh path.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_as_rates`: contributes all-strength supplementary rates such as `shots_per_60`, `ixg_per_60`, and `toi_per_gp`; metric families depending on it are weighted `/60` fallback and TOI fallback; classification is fallback / supplementary; quirks are rates must never override direct raw totals and can reconstruct numerators only when raw counts are absent; freshness dependency matters for fallback-heavy players; no writer was found in the inspected surface, so the runbook must document the current NST rates refresh path.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_as_counts_oi`: contributes all-strength on-ice counts and territorial context including GF, GA, SF, SA, zone starts, CF, CA, FF, and FA; metric families depending on it are on-ice context, possession / territorial, PDO, zone starts, and TOI secondary authority; classification is authoritative; quirks are on-ice TOI can also act as TOI authority when player counts TOI is absent; freshness dependency is critical for on-ice and territorial validation; no writer was found in the inspected surface, so the runbook must document the current NST on-ice counts refresh path.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_es_counts`: contributes EV player raw counts; metric families depending on it are EV surface stats, EV weighted `/60`, EV finishing, EV expected / chance; classification is authoritative; quirks mirror all-strength counts; freshness dependency is critical for EV audit; refresh path must be captured from the current NST ingest workflow.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_es_rates`: contributes EV supplementary rates and TOI fallback; metric families depending on it are EV weighted `/60` fallback and EV TOI fallback; classification is fallback / supplementary; quirks mirror all-strength rates; freshness dependency matters when EV raw counts or EV TOI are missing; refresh path must be captured from the current NST ingest workflow.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_es_counts_oi`: contributes EV on-ice counts and territorial context; metric families depending on it are EV on-ice context, EV possession / territorial, EV PDO, EV zone starts, and EV TOI secondary authority; classification is authoritative; quirks mirror all-strength on-ice counts; freshness dependency is critical for EV on-ice validation; refresh path must be captured from the current NST ingest workflow.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables
text: - `nst_gamelog_pp_counts`: contributes PP player raw counts; metric families depending on it are PP surface stats, PP weighted `/60`, PP finishing, PP expected / chance, and PP points; classification is authoritative; quirks are PP share does not come from this table and must stay separate from PP role context; freshness dependency is critical for PP scoring validation; refresh path must be captured from the current NST ingest workflow.

heading: 1. Upstream Tables

heading: Introduction/Overview
text: `/trends` is FHFH's movement-first analytics surface. It answers what is changing recently for teams, skaters, and goalies through comparable rolling windows, percentiles, ranks, risers/fallers, hot/cold direction, and concise short-horizon context. It must remain distinct from `/underlying-stats` (current-state intelligence and diagnosis) and `/trendsSandbox` (sustainability/expectation lab).

heading: Introduction/Overview
text: This PRD recovers the previously empty Trends scope from the Three Pillars PRD, rolling-player metrics contracts/remediation, the FORGE/Trends architecture, and current `/trends` code. Current implementation already contains team, skater, and goalie metric registries/APIs, CTPI, strength of schedule, Start Chart context, player detail, and section-level loading/error behavior. The initiative must verify those claims, close entity/data/ownership gaps, harden shared contracts and pagination, and provide a coherent production experience without absorbing deeper Sustainability or FORGE product ownership.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 1. `/trends` must support teams, skaters, and goalies as first-class entity sections with deliberate metric sets and explanations.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 2. Teams must expose movement for offense, defense, power play, penalty kill, pace/control, and other approved team categories with current and previous rank/percentile.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 3. Skaters must expose recent movement across approved production, shot/xG, playmaking, deployment/usage, physical, defensive/context, and luck/regression metrics when source coverage exists.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 4. Goalies must expose recent save quality, workload/share, goals saved/expected context, start-role context, and volatility/confidence without treating starter probability as performance.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 5. Each metric definition must specify entity, key, label, directionality, source fields/grain, units, window semantics, minimum sample, availability, and explanation.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 6. Rolling windows must follow each entity's actual games/observations as documented and use strict as-of ordering; player windows must not silently become team schedule windows.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 7. API outputs must include selected window, current value/rank/percentile, prior comparison point, delta, games/TOI/sample, source date/generated time, season, and warnings.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 8. Percentile direction must be normalized so higher displayed percentile consistently means better after lower-is-better handling.

heading: Functional Requirements
text: 9. Small/partial samples must produce confidence/insufficiency warnings and must not be presented as equally reliable to qualified samples.

heading: xG and GSAx architecture
text: That has direct schema implications. If you want **xS%**, **SAX%**, **unexpected goals**, **steal games**, **pressure-split goaltending**, **shot quantity versus shot quality team style**, **coach shot maps**, or a trustworthy **luck score**, you need canonical shot rows and not just aggregated game or season tables. MoneyPuck defines expected goals against as the sum of the expected goal values of unblocked shots faced and defines GSAx as expected goals against minus actual goals allowed. Evolving-Hockey also explains why blocked shots should not be treated as ordinary xG observations: the coordinates for blocked attempts are recorded where the shot was blocked, not where it was taken, so using blocked events naively would contaminate any shot-quality model. citeturn8view6turn8view1turn23view0
